statements that involve substantial risks and uncertainties. Other than statements of historical fact, all statements in this Registration

prospects, plans, and management objectives, are forward-looking statements. The words &ldquo;anticipate,&rdquo; &ldquo;believe,&rdquo;
&ldquo;estimate,&rdquo; &ldquo;expect,&rdquo; &ldquo;intend,&rdquo; &ldquo;may,&rdquo; &ldquo;plan,&rdquo; &ldquo;predict,&rdquo; &ldquo;project,&rdquo;

and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements, although not all forward-looking statements contain these
identifying words.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may not achieve the plans, intentions, or expectations
disclosed in our forward-looking statements, and you should not place undue reliance on our forward-looking statements. Actual results
or events could differ materially from the plans, intentions, and expectations disclosed in the forward-looking statements we make. We
have included important cautionary statements in this Registration Statement that we believe could cause actual results or events to differ
materially from the forward-looking statements we make. Our forward-looking statements do not reflect the potential impact of any future
acquisitions, mergers, dispositions, joint ventures, or investments we may make.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">You should read this Registration Statement and
the documents that we have filed as exhibits to this Registration Statement with the understanding that our actual future results may
be materially different from what we expect. The forward-looking statements in this Registration Statement are made as of the date of
this Registration Statement, and we do not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required by applicable

we will begin to file reports, proxy statements, information statements, and other information with the SEC. You may read and copy this

the SEC at&nbsp;1-800-SEC-0330 for more information on its Public Reference Room. Our SEC filings will also be available to the public
from commercial document retrieval services and at the website maintained by the SEC at http://www.sec.gov.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our Internet website address is http://americanantimony.com.
Information contained on the website does not constitute part of this Registration Statement. We have included our website address in
this Registration Statement solely as an inactive textual reference. When this Registration Statement is effective, we will make available,
through a link to the SEC&rsquo;s website, electronic copies of the materials we file with the SEC, including Annual Reports on Form 10-K,
Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, the Section 16 reports filed by our executive officers, directors, and 5%
stockholders and amendments to those reports.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="a_013"></A>ITEM 1. BUSINESS.</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><B>Overview</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We are incorporated in the State of Wyoming and
in good standing. We are engaged in the exploration and evaluation of antimony mineral properties in the United States. The Company holds
a portfolio comprised of three properties totaling 301 mining claims and approximately 6,219 acres. The Company has not reported mineral
resources or mineral reserves determined in accordance with Regulation S-K Subpart 1300. The Company is therefore an exploration-stage
issuer under that regulation. Exploration results, historical workings and metallurgical results, do not by themselves demonstrate economic
viability.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Business </B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We are incorporated in the State of Wyoming and
in good standing. Our website is, http//americanantimony.com or http//xtraenegy.com. We are in the business of mineral exploration and
mining. On April 12, 2022, we entered into a Service Agreement with Red Beryl Mining Inc. and Strategic Stibium Mining LLC (<FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">See
Exhibit 10.1</FONT>). The transaction closed on September 21, 2022. The consideration that was paid was 20,000,000 (twenty million) shares
of Common Stock of American Antimony Corporation (dba Xtra Energy Corporation).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>The American Antimony Project &ndash; Bernice
Canyon</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s American Antimony Project, located
in Bernice Canyon, Churchill County, Nevada, consists of 201 mining claims covering approximately 4,153 acres, or 6.49 square miles. The
Company initially acquired 40 mining claims encompassing approximately 825 acres and subsequently expanded its landholdings through the
acquisition of an additional 161 claims covering approximately 3,328 acres. (See Claim Map Below.)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The primary mineral commodity targeted by the
Company&rsquo;s exploration activities is antimony, a strategically important industrial metalloid used in various applications, including batteries,
semiconductors, flame retardants, paints, enamels, and other industrial products.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The project area contains eleven (11) historically
producing mines located within the Company&rsquo;s claim boundaries. These Past producing mines are named; The Arrance Mine; Antimony King;
King Solomon; IHX; Blue Eagle Group; Drumm Mine; Margueritte; Lofthouse Mine; the Hoyt; No-Name and U-Bet Mines. Although these historical
mining operations indicate previous mineral extraction activities in the area, they do not establish the existence of economically recoverable
mineral resources or mineral reserves under Regulation S-K Subpart 1300.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s principal objective is to conduct
systematic exploration and evaluation activities to determine whether its mining claims contain mineral deposits that may ultimately support
commercially viable mining operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has completed the first phase of its
planned multi-phase drilling and exploration program. Based on the preliminary results of this program, management believes that additional
exploration is warranted and is preparing for the second phase of drilling. Future exploration activities are expected to focus on further
evaluating mineralization, defining the extent and continuity of potential mineralized zones, and gathering additional geological and
technical information necessary to assess the project&rsquo;s development potential.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Notwithstanding the results of the initial drilling
program, substantial additional exploration, drilling, sampling, metallurgical testing, and engineering studies will be required before
the Company can determine whether economically viable mineral resources or mineral reserves exist. Any future determination of mineral
resources or reserves will require appropriate technical evaluation and supporting documentation in accordance with applicable SEC mining
disclosure requirements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>The Company has not established any mineral
resources or mineral reserves at the American Antimony Project in accordance with Regulation S-K Subpart 1300.</B> Accordingly, the property
remains an exploration-stage property, and there can be no assurance that the Company&rsquo;s ongoing exploration activities will result in
the identification of commercially viable mineral deposits or the commencement of profitable mining operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s exploration activities may also
be subject to seasonal weather conditions. Snowfall and adverse weather during winter months may temporarily restrict access to portions
of the property, potentially limiting field exploration and drilling activities to approximately ten months per year, depending on prevailing
weather and site conditions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company intends to continue its multi-phase
exploration program, subject to the availability of financing, regulatory approvals, contractor availability, and the results of ongoing
geological and technical evaluations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Location and Access to the American Antimony
Project</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The American Antimony Project is located in Bernice
Canyon, Churchill County, Bernice Mining District approximately 70km/42 miles northeast of Fallon Nevada and has GPS coordinates of 39&deg;
45&rsquo; 46&rsquo;&rsquo; North, 117&deg; 47&rsquo;16&rsquo;&rsquo; West, in the north central portion of Churchill County and has an elevation of 1,337 meters or 4,386
feet above sea level. The claims may be accessed by Federal Highway (paved), to a County Road to BLM road (2-lane, dirt), with the last
1.75 miles (single lane dirt/gravel) to the beginning of the canyon where the claims are. This is fairly rough and recommend 4-wheel drive.
Even though the terrain is semi-arid the claims may not be accessible all year round. There may be periods where our claims may be un-accessible
each year due to snow in the area. This means that our exploration activities could be limited to a period of about ten months to eleven
months per year.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>American Antimony Project Description</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The American Antimony Project mining claims are
unencumbered and in good standing with the BLM (Bureau of Land Management) and with Churchill County. There are no third-party conditions
which affect the claims other than conditions defined by the State of Nevada as, to permitting, and environmental reclamation. The claims
cover an area of 4,153 acres or 6.489 square miles. There is no insurance covering the claims. We believe that no insurance is necessary
since the claims are unimproved and contain no buildings or improvements and contains no infrastructure on the claims. The claim numbers,
registered owner number, expiry date, number of units, and work requirements are typically recorded with the BLM (Bureau of Land Management)
and Churchill County.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Conditions to Retain Title to our Mining Claims</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">In
order to retain title to the mining claims, we are required to pay annual maintenance fees on the claims to the BLM and Churchill County
in the amount totaling approximately $40,200 to the BLM by September 1, 2027, and approximately $9,000 to Churchill County due on or before
October 31, 2027. There are no other requirements to </FONT>retain title to the American Antimony Project. The claims are currently in
good standing until September 1, 2027, and October 31, 2027, at that time the annual maintenance fees are due to the BLM and Churchill
County Nevada.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Geology of Mining Claims</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Jungo Terrane - Turbiditic, fine-grained, terrigenous
clastic rocks</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Age: </B>Mesozoic (163.5 - 227 Ma)</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Stratigraphic Name: </B>Grass Valley Formation;
Happy Creek Volcanic Complex; Osobb Formation; Winnemucca Formation; Raspberry Formation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Description: </B>The Jungo terrane, also
called the Lovelock assemblage or Fencemaker allochthon (Oldow, Satterfield, and Silberling, 1993), consists of complexly deformed,
thick basinal, turbiditic, fine-grained, terrigenous clastic rocks, mainly Norian, but also as young as Pliensbachian (Late Triassic
and Early Jurassic) age. It crops out in southern Washoe, Churchill, Humboldt, and Pershing Counties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">These rocks represent the basinal facies component
of the Auld Lang Syne Group (Burke and Silberling, 1973; Lupe and Silberling, 1985). The Jungo terrane has no known basement and is structurally
detached from coeval shelf facies (Silberling, Jones, and others, 1992). It is locally overlain unconformably by Middle or Upper Jurassic
peritidal sedimentary rocks (Jcg) intruded by a gabbroic igneous assemblage (Silberling, 1991).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Rocks included with the Jungo terrane were
originally mapped as the Grass Valley Formation of the Auld Lang Syne Group in Humboldt and Pershing Counties; some rocks were
mapped as the Happy Creek Volcanic &ldquo;series&rdquo; (now the Happy Creek Volcanic Complex) in Humboldt County, the Nightingale
sequence in southern Washoe County, the Osobb Formation of the Auld Lang Syne Group in Churchill County, and the Winnemucca and
Raspberry Formations of the Auld Lang Syne Group (Compton, 1960) in the Santa Rosa Range in Humboldt County.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Comments: </B>Original map source: Crafford,
A.E.J., 2007, Geologic Map of Nevada: U.S. Geological Survey Data Series 249, 1 CD-ROM, 46 p., 1 plate; Scale 1:250,000.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Lithology: </B>Major:{siliciclastic}</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Reference: </B>Horton, J.D., C.A. San
Juan, and D.B. Stoeser. The State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC) geodatabase of the conterminous United States. doi:
10.3133/ds1052. U.S. Geological Survey Data Series 1052.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 7 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="width: 33%">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->4<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD><TD STYLE="width: 33%; text-align: right">&nbsp;</TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>History of Bernice Canyon/Bernice Mining District</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The historical account records that Wallace Goodell
located a quartz mining claim in 1881. Warren W. Williams and George W. Williams became involved in the property in 1883 and pursued development
of the quartz workings and associated milling operations. By 1884, Bernice had developed into a small mining settlement with a mill, stores,
residences and community services. The narrative identifies workings including the Golden Crown, Curtis, Williams and Lower tunnels. The
Williams brothers&rsquo; quartz mining and milling operations encountered technical and financial difficulties and were closed by 1888,
although other activity continued in the area. <B>[1]</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Willard Millery&rsquo;s article, &ldquo;Antimony
Veins at Bernice, Nevada,&rdquo; published April 15, 1916, identifies the Antimony King Mine at Bernice and the Lofthouse Mine approximately
five miles southeast as producing mines at that time. The article describes stibnite mineralization associated with quartz-filled fissures,
slate and limestone, with oxidized antimony minerals in weathered zones. At the Antimony King vein, the article reports a traceable fissure
and a lower drift extending approximately 200 feet; reported mineralized widths vary substantially. These descriptions concern historical
occurrences and are not contemporary verification of grade or continuity. <B>[2]</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Consulting geologist David Le Count Evans inspected
the Howard Turley antimony properties on July 9, 1970, and issued a memorandum on July 19, 1970. He described fifteen mining claims extending
approximately 15,000 feet along Bernice Canyon and observed narrow stibnite veins together with disseminated mineralization in latite
dikes and sills and adjoining sedimentary rocks. The author explicitly characterized the reconnaissance as preliminary and incomplete
and recommended further sampling, surveying, mapping, metallurgical work and geological testing. <B>[3]</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The 1970 memorandum reports that antimony was
discovered in the district in 1885, with production beginning in 1892 and shipments continuing through 1896. It also reports periods of
production during World War I, World War II and the Korean War, and states that the district had produced more than 300 tons of antimony
metal. These are historical assertions from the memorandum and have not been independently verified. <B>[3]</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Taken together, the documents establish a historical
record of quartz and antimony exploration, underground workings, intermittent antimony production, and renewed commercial interest through
the late 1960s. They do not establish present-day economic viability, mineral resources, mineral reserves, or ownership of the historical
workings by the present issuer.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>References</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

Pieplow, &ldquo;Bernice, Nevada: Once the Largest Town in Churchill County,&rdquo; </SUP></P>



<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><SUP>[2] Willard Millery, &ldquo;Antimony Veins at
Bernice, Nevada,&rdquo; Mining and Scientific Press, April 15, 1916,</SUP></P>

Antimony Properties, Bernice Canyon, Churchill County, Nevada,&rdquo; memorandum report, July 19, 1970</SUP></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Exploration Expenditures, Drilling Results, Activities
and Further Development</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of November 6, 2026 we have made expenditures
in regard to the actual exploration of the American Antimony Project mining claims in the amount of $790,184, This comprised of road work,
reverse circulation drilling, geological and engineering supervision, sampling, laboratory assays, additional surveying and sampling.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Results of Phase One Drilling Program</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">During the summer of
2025, the Company completed 14 reverse circulation (RC) drill holes totaling approximately 5,570 feet (1,697.7 meters), with individual
hole depths ranging from approximately 300 to 800 feet (91 to 244 meters).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Ten of the fourteen drill
holes intersected the targeted felsite dike, providing additional geological information concerning the distribution and potential continuity
of the targeted structure.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Selected drill holes
returned elevated antimony and gold assay results, including an approximately 87-meter mineralized interval in drill hole BC25-03 averaging
1.46% antimony, with a maximum reported assay of 5.59% antimony.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The results provide a
technical basis for additional drilling and geological investigations intended to further evaluate the lateral and vertical extent, grade
distribution, and geological characteristics of the identified mineralization.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Although the initial
drilling results are encouraging, the Company has not completed sufficient drilling or technical evaluation to establish mineral resources
or mineral reserves in accordance with Regulation S-K Subpart 1300.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Key Intercepts (Certified Lab Assays)</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%; font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">BC25-03 - Arrance Core Zone, 87 m (285 ft) continuous
felsite-hosted mineralization (103.6-190.5 m). Average 1.46% Sb (14,600 ppm), up to 5.59% Sb, with many in-situ assays between 2%-3% Sb.
Gold up to 1.33 g/t Au; average 0.27 g/t Au across the interval. This confirms vertical continuity of mineralization to a 500 ft depth.</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD></TD><TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">BC25-11 - Central Corridor12.3 m @ 1.06% Sb and
0.18 g/t Au (134.1-146.4 m). This supports increasing grade and thickness with depth.</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD></TD><TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">BC25-02 - Arrance (Lower Adit)7.6 m @ 1.08% Sb
with gold showings. The first laboratory-confirmed Sb intercept of the program.</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD></TD><TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">BC25-05 - Arrance True Width Test7.6 m @ 0.72%
Sb and 0.33 g/t Au. This confirms true dike width ~25 ft (7.6 m).</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD></TD><TD><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">BC25-01 &amp; BC25-04 - Peripheral Step-Outs
Sb assays up to 0.39% Sb (3,893 ppm) with gold up to 0.43 g/t. This confirms zoning and southern strike continuity.</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in">*<SUP>SB- Stibnite antimony
host rock</SUP></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in"><SUP>*AU- Gold</SUP></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.25in"><SUP></SUP>&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Independent Metallurgical Testing and Processing
Evaluation</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">As part of its continuing
technical evaluation of the American Antimony Project, the Company initiated an independent metallurgical testing program through ALS
Metallurgy to evaluate the processing characteristics of antimony-bearing material collected from the Company&rsquo;s historical mining areas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 9 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><TD STYLE="width: 33%">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->6<!-- Field: /Sequence --></TD><TD STYLE="width: 33%; text-align: right">&nbsp;</TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><P STYLE="margin: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The program included
approximately 400 kilograms (880 pounds) of bulk sample material obtained from the Antimony King historical stockpile and submitted for
independent laboratory evaluation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The primary objectives
of the metallurgical program were to evaluate the antimony content of the sampled material, assess its mineral processing characteristics,
and determine the potential for producing an antimony concentrate through laboratory-scale processing methods.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Preliminary laboratory
results reported antimony concentrate grades reaching approximately 63% Sb, with reported metallurgical recovery approaching 97% under
the specific laboratory test conditions evaluated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">These findings provide
additional technical information concerning the processing characteristics of the sampled material and may assist the Company in evaluating
potential future mineral processing alternatives.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company intends to
incorporate the metallurgical results into its continuing evaluation of the American Antimony Project, including additional sampling,
engineering studies, and assessment of potential processing methods.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The results are specific
to the samples and laboratory conditions evaluated and should not be interpreted as representative of the entire Antimony King stockpile
or the broader American Antimony Project. The Company has not established commercial processing economics, economically recoverable mineral
resources, or mineral reserves.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><B><I>Initial Resource
Definition and Development Strategy</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Following completion
of its Phase I reverse circulation drilling program and subsequent geological, metallurgical, engineering, and permitting evaluations,
the Company selected the historical Arrance Mine and the mineralized corridor extending toward the Antimony King Mine as the primary focus
of its initial resource-definition and potential development activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Arrance-to-Antimony
King corridor extends approximately 0.67 miles (1.07 kilometers) along an interpreted antimony-bearing felsite dike trend within the Company&rsquo;s
American Antimony Project in Bernice Canyon, Nevada.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The selection of the
Arrance area was based on several technical and operational considerations, including results from the Company&rsquo;s Phase I drilling program,
historical underground exposures, surface and underground sampling, geological mapping, existing access, previously disturbed working
areas, preliminary engineering evaluations, and consultations with permitting specialists.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">At the Arrance Mine,
historical underground workings provide access to portions of the mineralized geological system. Sampling of the exposed mineralized dike
within the lower adit has returned selected antimony assays of up to approximately 31% Sb. These results represent individual samples
and should not be interpreted as representative average grades of the broader mineralized structure.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 10 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->7<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company&rsquo;s 2025 drilling
program provided additional geological information supporting further evaluation of the Arrance area. Drill hole BC25-03 intersected approximately
87 meters (285 feet) of reported mineralization averaging 1.46% antimony, including individual assays reaching 5.59% antimony. Additional
drill holes, including BC25-02, BC25-05, and BC25-10, provided information concerning antimony mineralization and the geometry of the
targeted geological structures.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Based on these results,
the Company&rsquo;s initial development strategy is focused on advancing additional resource-definition drilling, geological modeling, bulk
sampling, metallurgical evaluation, engineering studies, and applicable small-mine permitting activities within the Arrance-to-Antimony
King corridor.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company intends to
evaluate the potential for initial small-scale antimony mining and concentrate production, subject to the results of additional technical
studies, financing, regulatory approvals, and commercial considerations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company continues
to evaluate additional historical mines, prospects, stockpiles, and mineralized structures throughout its broader Bernice Canyon property
position. These district-scale activities are intended to identify potential future exploration and development opportunities beyond the
initial Arrance-to-Antimony King focus area.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company has not established
mineral resources or mineral reserves in accordance with Regulation S-K Subpart 1300, completed a feasibility study, or demonstrated that
commercial mining or processing operations would be economically viable. The Company&rsquo;s development objectives remain subject to substantial
geological, technical, regulatory, financial, and operational uncertainties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white"><B><I>Road Restoration
and District-Wide Access</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company has undertaken
a phased program to evaluate and improve access to historical mining and exploration areas throughout Bernice Canyon.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Phase I road restoration
activities established improved access through the Company&rsquo;s principal Antimony King, King Solomon, and Arrance exploration areas, supporting
ongoing geological investigations and preliminary development planning.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The Company is also evaluating
a proposed Phase II rehabilitation program involving existing historical mining roads extending toward additional former producing areas,
including Hoyt, U-Bet, Marguerite, Drumm, and Blue Eagle.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The proposed program
is intended to improve access across approximately 3.5 miles of historical mineralized strike, supporting future geological mapping, sampling,
exploration drilling, stockpile evaluation, and infrastructure planning.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The proposed Phase II
activities remain subject to applicable regulatory approvals, financing, site conditions, and operational requirements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Costs and Effects of Compliance with Environmental
Laws</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We currently have currently posted a surety bond
in the amount of $20,000 to comply with environmental laws concerning our exploration program. We will encounter further costs associated
with the continuing development of the American Antimony Project, where we will be required to file a plan of remediation with the BLM
and the State of Nevada in the event the ground has been disturbed. and can be returned to its near original form in compliance with the
BLM and the State of Nevada.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Stibium Creek Prospect &ndash; Lander County,
Nevada</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In 2025 the Company acquired 60 Claims or 1,240
Acres in Lander County Nevada through staking the claims. This prospect is known as the Stibium Creek Prospect. Stibium Creek provides
the Company with an additional exploration opportunity in a documented past producing area. To date the Company has not conducted any
exploration activities on the Stibium Creek Prospect. <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">In order to retain title
to the mining claims, we are required to pay annual maintenance on the claims to the BLM and Lander County in the amount totaling approximately
$12,000 to the BLM by September 1, 2027, and approximately $2,687 to Lander County due on or before October 31, 2027. There are no other
requirements to </FONT>retain title to the Stibium Creek Prospect. The claims are currently in good standing until September 1, 2027,
and October 31, 2027, at that time the annual maintenance fees are due to the BLM and Lander County Nevada. Additionally, there are no
proven or probable reserves identified on the Stibium Creek Prospect.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Crystalite Prospect-Okanogan County, Washington</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In 2025 the Company acquired 40 Claims or 825
Acres in Okanogan County Washington through staking the claims. This prospect is known as the Crystalite Prospect. The Crystalite Prospect
provides the Company with an additional exploration opportunity in a documented past producing area. To date the Company has not conducted
any exploration activities on the Crystalite Prospect. <FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">In order to retain title
to the mining claims, we are required to pay annual maintenance on the claims to the BLM and Okanogan County in the amount totaling approximately
$8,000 to the BLM by September 1, 2027, and approximately $200 to Okanogan County due on or before October 31, 2027. There are no other
requirements to </FONT>retain title to the Crystalite Prospect. The claims are currently in good standing until September 1, 2027, and
October 31, 2027, at that time the annual maintenance fees are due to the BLM and Okanogan County Washington. Additionally, there are
no proven or probable reserves identified on the Crystalite Prospect.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Competitive Conditions</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The mineral exploration business is an extremely
competitive industry. We are competing with many other exploration companies looking for minerals. Being a junior mineral exploration
company, we compete with other companies like ours for financing and joint venture partners. Additionally, we compete for other resources
such as professional geologists, camp staff, helicopters and mineral exploration supplies.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Dependence on Major Customers</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We currently have no customers.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Intellectual Property </B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">We have registered the trademark and Logo &ldquo;American
Antimony&rdquo; internationally under the Madrid Protocol and the UK and Australia have accepted the trademark. We are currently waiting
for a response from the US patent and Trademark Office.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Government Approvals and Regulations</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We are required to comply with all regulations
defined by the State of Nevada Division of Minerals, the BLM and the Nevada Revised Statutes (NRS). The effect of these existing regulations
on our business is that we are able to carry out our exploration program as we have described in this Registration Statement. Additionally,
we are required to obtain permits for exploration activities commencing with, where we are required to file an exploration plan with State,
as well, file a plan of remediation with the BLM in the event the ground has been disturbed as well as post a surety bond. It is possible
that a future government could change the regulations that could limit our ability to explore our claims, but we believe this is unlikely.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left">&nbsp;</P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Employees</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We do not have any employees other than our officers
and directors. We retain the services of independent geologists, engineers, drilling crews, mining contractors, and other consultants
on a contract basis to conduct exploration activities on the American Antimony Project.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="a_014"></A>ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS.</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>An investment in our common stock involves
a high degree of risk. Investors should carefully consider the following risks together with the other information in this Registration
Statement. These risks could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, prospects and the value
of our common stock. Investors could lose some or all of their investment. Additional risks that we do not currently know about or consider
material may also adversely affect us. Certain statements in this section are forward-looking statements and are subject to the uncertainties
described below.</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Risks relating to our business and financing</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We have not generated mining revenues and
may never achieve profitable operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We are engaged primarily in acquiring, exploring
and evaluating mineral properties. We have not generated revenues from mining operations and cannot assure investors when, if ever, we
will generate material revenues from the extraction and sale of minerals. Our limited operating history does not provide a reliable basis
for evaluating our ability to establish a profitable mining business.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our ability to generate revenues depends on identifying
economically recoverable mineralization, obtaining permits, securing financing and successfully developing and operating our properties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We expect to incur operating losses while funding
exploration, technical studies and corporate activities. If these expenditures do not lead to profitable operations, we may exhaust our
available funds and be required to suspend or cease operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our need for additional financing creates
substantial uncertainty about our ability to continue operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our operations depend on financing rather than
internally generated mining revenues. Exploration, drilling, metallurgical testing, permitting, engineering, reclamation and potential
mine development require substantial capital. Our ability to continue as a going concern depends on obtaining adequate financing or generating
sufficient operating cash flows. There is no assurance that financing will be available when required or on acceptable terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If we cannot obtain sufficient funding, we may
be required to reduce, postpone or discontinue exploration and development, relinquish mineral interests, sell assets or cease operations.
Debt financing may impose repayment obligations and restrictive covenants. Strategic financing arrangements may require us to surrender
valuable project rights. Uncertainty about our ability to continue operations may make financing more difficult to obtain.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We may be unable to obtain a joint venture
partner and partnership arrangements may reduce our project interests</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may seek a joint venture or strategic partner
to fund further exploration or development. We compete with other exploration companies for partners, and our properties may not attract
investment on acceptable terms. A joint venture may require us to transfer a portion of our property interests, share control over development
decisions or accept commitments that limit our flexibility. A partner&rsquo;s failure to fund or perform its obligations, or disagreements
over project decisions, could delay development. If a necessary partner cannot be secured, we may be unable to advance a project.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>


<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 13 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->10<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
