<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Dependence on key personnel and limited
management availability could interrupt our operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our success depends on our management and our
ability to retain qualified geologists, engineers and other mining professionals. Certain officers and directors devote only part of their
time to our business and may have competing responsibilities. Limited availability, the loss of key personnel or difficulty recruiting
experienced professionals could delay decisions, interrupt exploration programs or impair our ability to execute our plans. Competition
for qualified mining personnel can also increase our costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We face substantial competition in the mining
industry</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The mineral exploration and mining industry is
highly competitive. We compete with numerous companies, many of which have substantially greater financial, technical and personnel resources
than we do. Competition exists for attractive mineral properties, financing, qualified personnel, contractors, equipment and access to
processing facilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We may acquire additional mineral properties
that prove unsuccessful or result in unanticipated liabilities</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may acquire additional mineral properties or
interests in mineral projects based on limited geological, technical, environmental or title information. Acquired properties may fail
to contain economically recoverable mineralization, may require greater expenditures than anticipated or may be subject to environmental,
title, regulatory or other liabilities that were not identified before acquisition. We may incur losses or impairment charges relating
to such properties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>The carrying values of our mineral properties
and equipment may be subject to impairment</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We capitalize certain costs associated with mineral
properties and other assets in accordance with applicable accounting requirements. Changes in exploration results, commodity prices, permitting
status, claim ownership, development plans, expected future cash flows or other circumstances may indicate that the carrying value of
an asset is not recoverable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If such circumstances arise, we may be required
to recognize an impairment charge, which could materially reduce our reported assets and increase our reported net loss.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our exploration and development plans are
based on assumptions that may change materially</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our budgets, schedules and development plans necessarily
rely upon assumptions regarding exploration results, commodity prices, financing availability, permitting timelines, contractor availability,
operating costs, metallurgical recoveries and other matters. Actual results may differ materially from those assumptions, and we may modify,
postpone or abandon exploration or development programs in response to changing circumstances.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Risks relating to exploration and mine development</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Exploration may not identify economically
recoverable deposits or establish mineral reserves</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Mineral exploration is speculative, and few explored
properties become operating mines. Our interpretation of geological, geophysical, geochemical, drilling and sampling information may prove
inaccurate.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Unexpected geological conditions, discontinuous
mineralization or inadequate grades may cause exploration expenditures to produce no commercially recoverable deposit.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 14 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->11<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may never establish proven or probable mineral
reserves on our properties. A mineral resource is not a mineral reserve and does not demonstrate economic viability. Additional exploration
and technical and economic studies are necessary before mineralization can be classified as a mineral reserve. Even encouraging exploration
results do not establish that a deposit is economically or legally mineable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Geological interpretations and any future
resource or reserve estimates may prove inaccurate</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our expectations concerning tonnage, grade, continuity
and recovery depend on the quality and interpretation of drilling, sampling, assays and other technical data. Actual conditions may differ
materially, and further exploration may require substantial revisions to earlier interpretations. Any future mineral resource or reserve
estimates would also depend on assumptions about commodity prices, operating costs, recoveries and other economic factors. Revised estimates
or unfavorable conditions could reduce project value or cause us to suspend or abandon development.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If we identify inferred mineral resources, they
would have a lower level of geological confidence than indicated or measured mineral resources. Inferred resources cannot be converted
directly into mineral reserves and should not be assumed to be economically or legally mineable. Further exploration may not upgrade them
to a higher classification.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Metallurgical testing and pilot operations
may not predict commercial performance</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Laboratory, bench, bulk-sample and pilot testing
may produce results that cannot be replicated under commercial operating conditions. Tested material may not represent the full deposit,
and differences in mineralogy, dilution, grade, equipment and processing methods may materially affect recoveries, concentrate quality,
reagent consumption and costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Bulk sampling, pilot mining or small-scale extraction
may help evaluate a project but does not establish that larger-scale production will be economically viable. Actual mining rates, grades,
recoveries and operating costs may differ substantially at commercial scale. Technical or economic problems identified during scale-up
could require additional investment, delay development or prevent commercial production.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>There is substantial uncertainty associated
with transitioning from exploration to commercial mining operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Even if exploration activities are successful,
developing a mine requires substantial additional work, including technical studies, engineering, metallurgical testing, permitting, financing,
construction, procurement and commissioning. Development costs and schedules are inherently uncertain. Actual capital expenditures, operating
costs, production rates and recoveries may differ materially from estimates. We have limited experience operating commercial mining operations,
and there can be no assurance that we will successfully transition from exploration to development or production.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Volatile antimony prices could make our
projects uneconomic</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The economic viability of our mineral properties
depends substantially upon market prices for the commodities that we seek to explore and develop, including antimony.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Commodity prices are subject to significant fluctuations
resulting from factors beyond our control, including global supply and demand, economic conditions, industrial demand, technological developments,
substitution of materials, recycling, geopolitical events, trade restrictions, tariffs, government policies, interest rates, currency
exchange rates and speculative activity. A significant or sustained decline in applicable commodity prices could make exploration or development
uneconomic, reduce the value of our properties, result in impairment charges, make financing more difficult to obtain or cause us to delay,
suspend or abandon a project.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We depend upon third-party contractors and
consultants to conduct significant portions of our operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We rely upon independent geologists, engineers,
drilling contractors, laboratories, metallurgical consultants, mining contractors, environmental consultants and other third parties to
conduct significant aspects of our exploration and development activities. Our operations could be adversely affected if these parties
fail to perform their obligations, experience financial difficulties, provide inaccurate or incomplete information, fail to comply with
applicable laws or are unavailable when required.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 15 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->12<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We may encounter shortages or increased
costs of equipment, supplies, labor and services</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The mining industry may experience periods of
increased demand for drilling rigs, heavy equipment, qualified personnel, explosives, fuel, laboratory services, contractors and other
supplies and services. Shortages, supply-chain disruptions or price increases could materially increase our exploration and development
costs or delay planned activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our properties may lack the infrastructure
necessary for commercial mining operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The development of a mineral property may require
access roads, electrical power, water supplies, processing facilities, transportation facilities and other infrastructure. Existing infrastructure
at or near our properties may be inadequate to support commercial mining operations. Construction or improvement of infrastructure may
require substantial capital expenditures, governmental approvals and agreements with third parties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Water availability and water rights may
affect the feasibility of developing our properties</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Mining and mineral processing may require significant
quantities of water. Water availability in parts of the western United States is limited and subject to competing demands. We may be required
to acquire or obtain rights to sufficient water supplies for future operations. Water shortages, drought, regulatory restrictions or competing
uses could adversely affect the feasibility or cost of developing a mining operation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We may not be able to economically process
or market minerals recovered from our properties</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Even if we successfully extract mineralized material,
we may require third-party processing, milling, smelting, refining or transportation services. The availability and cost of such services
could affect project economics. We may also encounter penalties or restrictions associated with impurities or other characteristics of
concentrates or other mineral products. Suitable processing facilities or purchasers may not be available on acceptable commercial terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Operational hazards and insufficient insurance
could expose us to substantial losses</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Exploration, development and mining involve accidents,
equipment failures, ground instability, cave-ins, rock falls, fires, flooding, transportation incidents, pollution and injuries to personnel.
These events could cause personal injury or death, property or environmental damage, litigation, enforcement actions or suspension of
operations. Insurance may be unavailable for certain hazards, prohibitively expensive or insufficient to cover a loss. Uninsured losses,
deductibles and costs exceeding policy limits could materially impair our liquidity and ability to continue operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Severe weather and natural events may restrict
access and interrupt operations</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Snow, extreme temperatures, drought, flooding,
wildfires and storms may restrict access to our properties, damage equipment or infrastructure and reduce the availability of water. Seasonal
limitations can reduce the time available for fieldwork. These events may increase costs, delay exploration and development or cause prolonged
suspension of operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Risks relating to mineral rights and regulation</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our mineral claims may be subject to title
defects, competing claims or challenges to their validity</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our interests in mineral properties may consist
in whole or in part of unpatented mining claims or other mineral rights. The validity and ownership of such interests may be uncertain
and may be affected by compliance with federal and state laws, claim location procedures, annual maintenance requirements, recording requirements
and other matters. Our mineral interests may also be subject to conflicting claims, boundary disputes, overlapping claims, prior rights,
easements, rights-of-way or other title defects. If our title to a material portion of a property is successfully challenged, we could
lose some or all of our interest in that property.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 16 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->13<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Failure to maintain our claims could result
in loss of mineral rights</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our mineral claims are subject to annual maintenance
payments, recording requirements and other actions necessary to remain in good standing. Failure to make a required payment or filing
on time, or an error in claim records, could cause a claim to become void, abandoned or available for relocation by another party.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Increases in claim maintenance fees or difficulties
confirming claim status could also increase our costs. Loss of material claims could prevent exploration or development and require us
to write off related costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Some of our properties may be affected by
land-use restrictions, protected areas or other limitations on mineral activities</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Federal and state land-management decisions may
restrict or prohibit mineral exploration or development in certain areas. Our claims could be affected by wilderness designations, wilderness
study areas, protected habitats, cultural or archaeological resources, withdrawal of lands from mineral entry or other land-use restrictions.
If a portion of one of our properties is determined to be located within an area where activities are restricted or prohibited, we may
be unable to explore or develop that portion and may be required to impair or write off related property costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We may be unable to obtain or maintain the
permits and governmental approvals required for exploration, development and mining</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our activities are subject to federal, state and
local laws and regulations governing mineral exploration, mining, land use, environmental protection, water use, reclamation, air quality,
wildlife, cultural resources and occupational health and safety. Our ability to conduct exploration activities and ultimately develop
mining operations may depend upon obtaining and maintaining permits, authorizations and approvals from governmental agencies. Required
permits may be delayed, denied, challenged, modified, suspended or made subject to conditions that materially increase our costs or restrict
our activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Environmental laws and regulations may impose
significant costs and liabilities on us</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our exploration and potential mining activities
are subject to extensive environmental regulation concerning, among other matters, surface disturbance, water quality, air quality, waste
disposal, hazardous substances, wildlife, vegetation, cultural resources and reclamation. Environmental requirements may become more stringent
over time. We may also become responsible for environmental conditions associated with properties that existed before we acquired an interest
in them. Compliance obligations and environmental liabilities could be significant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our reclamation obligations could be significant
and actual reclamation costs may exceed our estimates</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Exploration and mining activities generally create
obligations to reclaim disturbed land. Regulatory authorities may require reclamation bonds, surety bonds, letters of credit or other
financial assurances. Estimates of reclamation costs may differ materially from actual costs as a result of changes in regulatory requirements,
site conditions, inflation, contractor costs or the scope of required reclamation activities. Increased financial assurance or reclamation
requirements could adversely affect our liquidity.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Changes in mining laws and government policies
may increase costs or restrict development</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Federal, state and local laws and policies govern
mineral tenure, land access, permitting, environmental protection, taxation, royalties, workplace safety and reclamation. Changes in laws,
agency interpretations or court decisions may impose additional obligations, increase costs, delay approvals or make a project uneconomic.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our activities on federal lands may be affected
by changes to claim maintenance fees, royalties, environmental review, reclamation requirements or mineral entry and access rules. Restrictions
on federal lands could reduce the area available for exploration or prevent development of a property.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our operations could be affected by disputes,
litigation or regulatory proceedings</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Mineral exploration and mining activities can
result in disputes concerning property ownership, claim validity, boundaries, contracts, environmental matters, permitting, access rights,
employment matters or other issues. Litigation and regulatory proceedings can be costly and time consuming, regardless of their outcome.
An adverse determination could result in monetary damages, loss of mineral rights, restrictions on operations or other material consequences.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->14<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Mining disclosure requirements and weaknesses
in technical reporting controls could increase costs and cause inaccurate disclosures</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our SEC mining disclosures must comply with applicable
requirements of Regulation S-K Subpart 1300. Compliance may require qualified persons to prepare or review technical information and,
when required, technical report summaries for material properties. Additional drilling, sampling, metallurgical testing or studies may
be needed before particular information can be disclosed. This work may be costly and time consuming. Deficiencies in collecting, validating
or reviewing technical information could result in inaccurate or incomplete disclosures, regulatory comments, amended filings or other
adverse consequences. Such deficiencies could damage investor confidence and hinder our ability to obtain financing.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Risks relating to reporting and corporate
governance</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Limited accounting resources and segregation
of duties may prevent timely detection of errors or fraud</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our small staff and limited accounting resources
restrict segregation of duties and independent review. Weaknesses in cash controls, financial reporting review or information technology
controls could permit errors, unauthorized transactions or fraud to go undetected. Inadequate backup or protection of financial records
and material agreements could also disrupt reporting.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If our controls fail to prevent or detect material
misstatements on a timely basis, we may need to correct or restate financial statements or amend SEC filings. Remediation may require
personnel and systems expenditures that strain our resources. These problems could expose us to regulatory proceedings or litigation,
undermine investor confidence and impair access to capital.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>SEC reporting and governance requirements
will increase costs and demands on management</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Becoming an SEC reporting company will increase
our legal, accounting, compliance and administrative expenses. Preparing periodic reports, maintaining disclosure controls and meeting
applicable internal control requirements will require management time and resources that would otherwise be available for exploration
and development.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Director and officer liability insurance may also
become more costly or provide limited coverage, making it harder to recruit and retain qualified directors and officers. If we cannot
meet our reporting obligations accurately and on time, we could face regulatory action, loss of investor confidence and reduced financing
opportunities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Reduced disclosure requirements may limit
information available to investors</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">To the extent we qualify as a smaller reporting
company or emerging growth company, we may use applicable scaled disclosure requirements, including reduced executive compensation disclosures.
Depending on our filer status and available exemptions, our independent registered public accounting firm may not be required to attest
to the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. These exemptions do not eliminate applicable management certification,
disclosure control or management internal control responsibilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Reduced disclosures or the absence of an auditor
attestation may make it harder for investors to assess our financial condition and controls or compare us with other reporting companies.
Investors may find our securities less attractive, which could reduce liquidity and adversely affect our stock price.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Indemnification and limits on director liability
could create expenses and reduce stockholder remedies</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our governing documents and applicable law may
provide indemnification, advancement of expenses and limitations on director liability. To the extent applicable, these provisions may
require us to spend substantial amounts defending or resolving claims involving directors or officers. We may be unable to recover amounts
advanced, and insurance may not cover all costs.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Permitted limitations on liability may restrict
stockholders&rsquo; ability to recover monetary damages for certain conduct. These protections are subject to statutory limitations and
do not eliminate liability under applicable securities laws. The SEC has stated that indemnification for liabilities arising under the
Securities Act is against public policy and therefore unenforceable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Risks relating to our common stock</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Concentrated voting power may limit common
stockholders influence and discourage a change of control</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our officers, directors and affiliates may exercise
substantial influence over matters submitted to stockholders, including election of directors, mergers and other significant transactions.
The voting rights attached to our Series A Preferred Stock can concentrate control beyond the holders&rsquo; proportionate ownership of
common stock. Common stockholders may therefore have limited ability to affect our management or policies.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Controlling holders may have interests that differ
from those of other stockholders. Concentrated voting power and the absence of cumulative voting may delay or discourage a change of control,
including a transaction that could otherwise provide common stockholders with a premium. Conflicts over financing, related-party arrangements
or project decisions could adversely affect minority stockholders.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Preferred stock rights may reduce amounts
available to common stockholders</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our preferred stock may have rights and preferences
senior to our common stock, including voting and liquidation rights. Applicable liquidation preferences could substantially reduce or
eliminate distributions available to common stockholders in a liquidation, dissolution or winding up. Conversion of preferred stock into
common stock may also substantially dilute existing common stockholders. Investors should consider the preferred stock terms described
in the Description of Securities section of this Registration Statement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Additional securities issuances may substantially
dilute existing stockholders</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may issue common stock, preferred stock, convertible
securities, warrants or other equity-linked securities to finance operations, acquire properties or compensate service providers. New
issuances and conversions or exercises of outstanding securities may reduce existing stockholders&rsquo; ownership and voting percentages.
Securities issued in future transactions may have rights senior to those of common stock.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Significant dilution or the expectation of additional
issuances could reduce our stock price and make future financing more difficult or more dilutive. Our ability to raise funds through securities
issuances does not assure that financing will be available on favorable terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>An inactive trading market may prevent investors
from selling their shares</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">A liquid and active market for our common stock
may not develop or be sustained. Trading may be limited or sporadic, with few buyers at a given time and substantial differences between
bid and ask prices. Limited investor awareness and research coverage may further reduce market activity. Investors may be unable to sell
shares when desired, at quoted prices or at all. Even relatively small sales may adversely affect the market price.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Our stock price may be volatile and substantial
sales could depress the market price</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our stock price may fluctuate significantly in
response to exploration and metallurgical results, financing announcements, permitting decisions, commodity prices, changes in management,
litigation, market conditions and other events. Price and trading volume changes may be unrelated to our operating performance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Penny stock requirements may limit broker
participation and make our shares harder to sell</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">To the extent our common stock is subject to the
SEC&rsquo;s penny stock rules, broker-dealers may be required to provide specified disclosures, determine suitability, approve accounts
and obtain written agreements before certain transactions. These requirements are subject to exceptions and may discourage broker-dealers
from recommending or effecting transactions in our shares. Reduced broker participation could limit trading, increase transaction costs
and make shares difficult to sell.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Statutory protection for forward looking
statements may be unavailable</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The statutory safe harbors for forward-looking
statements under the federal securities laws exclude certain issuers and transactions, including statements by issuers of penny stocks.
To the extent those exclusions apply to us, we may not be able to rely on these safe harbors in litigation concerning projections or other
forward-looking statements. Defending such claims could be expensive and divert management resources even if we ultimately prevail.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>We do not expect to pay cash dividends</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We have not paid cash dividends on our common
stock and expect to retain any future earnings to fund operations and development. Any future dividend would depend on our earnings, financial
condition, financing restrictions and board decisions. Investors should not expect dividend income, and a return on investment would generally
depend on selling shares at a price above their acquisition cost. Our share price may never appreciate.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><A NAME="a_015"></A>ITEM 2. FINANCIAL INFORMATION.</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><U><A NAME="a_050"></A>Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis
of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</U></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The following discussion summarizes the significant
factors affecting the operating results, financial condition and liquidity, and cash flows of our company for the years ended December
31, 2025, and 2024 and the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. You should read this discussion together with the consolidated financial
statements, related notes, and other financial information included in this Form 10. Except for historical information, the matters discussed
in this Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations are forward-looking statements that
involve risks and uncertainties and are based upon judgments concerning various factors beyond our control. These risks could cause our
actual results to differ materially from any future performance suggested below.<B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Overview</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">American Antimony Corporation (dba Xtra Energy
Corporation) (&ldquo;<B>Xtra</B>,&rdquo; &ldquo;<B>XTPT</B>,&rdquo; &ldquo;<B>we</B>,&rdquo; &ldquo;<B>us</B>,&rdquo; or the &ldquo;<B>Company</B>&rdquo;)
was incorporated in Wyoming and in good standing. Our offices are located at <B>10900 Research Blvd, Suite 160C, Austin TX 78759 </B>The
telephone number at our principal executive offices is <B>512-412-3636. </B>Our website address is, http//americanantimony.com or http//xtraenegy.com.
Our email address is compliance@americantimony.com We do not incorporate the information on or accessible through our website into this
Registration Statement, and you should not consider any information on, or that can be accessed through, our website a part of this Registration
Statement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Management is highly experienced at business integration
and has relevant experience in the exploration and mining industry and three of our board members are Professional Engineers and hold
the P.ENG designation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>History</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We were incorporated in the State of Wyoming on,
under the name &ldquo;Xtra Energy Corporation.&rdquo; We were initially organized to develop and explore mineral properties in the State
of Nevada. Effective November 25, 2024, we changed our name to &ldquo;American Antimony Corporation with the State of Wyoming. To date
we have not received approval from FINRA to formally change the Company&rsquo;s name. We have one subsidiary incorporated in the State
of Nevada under the name &ldquo;American Antimony, Inc.&rdquo;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I></I></B></P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->17<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Critical Accounting Policies</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">This &ldquo;<A HREF="#a_050">Management&rsquo;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</A>&rdquo; section is based upon our financial statements, which have been prepared
in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&ldquo;<B>U.S. GAAP</B>&rdquo;). The preparation
of the financial statements requires that we make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, and
expenses, and related disclosures.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We base our estimates on historical experience,
performance metrics, and various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form
the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Actual results will differ from these estimates
under different assumptions or conditions. We apply the following critical accounting policies in the preparation of our consolidated
financial statements:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Use of Estimates</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The preparation of financial statements in conformity
with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure
of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and reported amounts of expenses during the reporting period.
Significant estimates and judgments include, among other matters, stock-based compensation, valuation of financial instruments, recoverability
of mineral property interests, and valuation allowances for deferred tax assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Management bases its estimates and assumptions
on current facts, historical experience and other factors believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ
materially from those estimates, and revisions to estimates are recognized prospectively in the period in which the estimates are revised.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Revenue Recognition</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with
Accounting Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;) 606, <I>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</I>. The core principle of ASC 606
is that revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration
to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company applies the following five-step model
in determining revenue recognition:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="width: 3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 3%">1.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 94%">Identify the contract with a customer;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">2.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Identify the performance obligations in the contract;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">3.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Determine the transaction price;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">4.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations; and</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">5.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Recognize revenue when, or as, the Company satisfies a performance obligation.</TD></TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The transaction price represents the amount of
consideration to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring promised goods or services to a customer. The transaction
price may include fixed consideration, variable consideration, or both. When determining the transaction price, the Company considers,
as applicable, variable consideration, constraints on variable consideration, significant financing components, noncash consideration,
and consideration payable to a customer.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 21 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->18<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Mineral and Antimony Sales</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">When the Company commences commercial production
and enters into contracts with customers for the sale of antimony or other mineral products, revenue will be recognized when control of
the products transfers to the customer in accordance with the applicable contractual terms. The transfer of control will generally occur
upon delivery of the mineral products to the customer or other point specified in the contract when the customer obtains the ability to
direct the use of and obtain substantially all of the remaining benefits from the products.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company will consider the specific terms of
each sales arrangement in determining the appropriate point of revenue recognition, including delivery terms, acceptance provisions, rights
of return, pricing provisions, and other contractual terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Variable Consideration</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Where consideration is subject to variability,
including adjustments based on the quantity, quality, grade, assay results, or other characteristics of mineral products, the Company
will estimate variable consideration in accordance with ASC 606 and include amounts in the transaction price only to the extent that it
is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur when the uncertainty is subsequently resolved.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Royalties, Streaming and Other Mineral-Related
Arrangements</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If the Company enters into royalty, streaming,
offtake, joint marketing, processing, or other arrangements involving mineral properties or mineral products, the Company will evaluate
each arrangement to determine whether it represents a contract with a customer within the scope of ASC 606 or is subject to other applicable
U.S. GAAP guidance. Revenue will be recognized based on the applicable accounting guidance and the specific contractual terms of the arrangement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Contract Balances</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Amounts received from customers before the Company
satisfies the related performance obligations will be recorded as contract liabilities or deferred revenue, as applicable. Amounts for
which the Company has an unconditional right to consideration will be recorded as accounts receivable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company had no revenue from contracts with
customers during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">See Note 2 of Notes to Financial Statements in
this Form 10 for management&rsquo;s discussion of recent accounting pronouncements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Results of Operations for the Fiscal Year
Ended December 31, 2025, Compared to the Fiscal Year Ended December 31, 2024, and the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Compared to the
Quarter Ended September 30, 2025.</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Operating Expenses</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>&nbsp;</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>General &amp; Administrative Expenses</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">General and administrative expenses include professional
fees, costs associated with exploration and development, press releases, travel, and other expenses. We incurred general and administrative
expenses of $738,327 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, versus $157,463 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, an increase
of $580,864 (386.89%). This increase was due to having significantly higher exploration costs and increased exploration activities in
2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 22 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center"><!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->19<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We incurred general and administrative expenses
of $147,564 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, versus $494,619 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $347,055
(70.17%) decrease was primarily due to decreased exploration costs and decreased exploration activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 117.5pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We incurred general and administrative expenses
of $263,209 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus $655,395 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The $392,186 (59.84%)
decrease was primarily due to decreased exploration costs and decreased exploration activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>Other Income (Expense)</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our other income and expenses include interest
expense only. We recognized other income and expenses of $32,412 (interest expense) for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, versus
other income and expenses of $16,045 (interest expense) for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. The increase of $16,367 (102%) was
due to higher interest expense.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our other income and expenses incurred were $9,128
for the three months ended September 30, 2026, versus other income and expenses of $8,180 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
The increase of $948 (10.39%) was primarily due to higher interest expense.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Our other income and expenses incurred were $26,986
for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus other income and expenses of $24,272 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
The increase of $2,714 (10.06%) was primarily due to higher interest expense in 2026.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>Net Losses</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>&nbsp;</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We incurred a net loss of $3,166,594 for the fiscal
year ended December 31, 2025, versus $332,408 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, representing a $2,834,186 (852.62%) increase.
This increase was attributed to increased exploration costs and the issuance of share-based compensation.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We incurred a net loss of $156,692 for the three
months ended September 30, 2026, versus a net loss of $1,552,739 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease
of $1,396,047 (790.95%). This decrease was attributed to the fact that we experienced higher operating expenses and exploration costs
in the quarter ending September 30, 2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We incurred a net loss of $290,195 for the nine
months ended September 30, 2026, versus a net loss of $3,075,522 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing a decrease
of $2,785,327 (959.81%). This decrease was attributed to the fact that we experienced higher operating expenses and exploration costs
during 2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I><U>Liquidity and Capital Resources</U></I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Operating Activities</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, we
used $760,260 of cash in operations, which included our net loss of $3,166,594 offset by a $2,395,856 in share-based compensation, a decrease
of prepaid expenses and other assets of $31,608 and an increase of accounts payable and accrued liabilities of $42,086. Cash flows remained
relatively consistent year-over-year but the increase in Net cash used in operating activities is primarily due to the increased exploration
and operating expenses.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">For the nine months ended September 30, 2026,
we used $257,126 of cash in operations, which included our net loss of $290,195 offset by a $2,627 decrease in prepaid expenses, an increase
of accounts payable and accrued liabilities of $32,626. The decrease in net cash used in operating activities is primarily due to the
decreased exploration and operating expenses.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Investing Activities</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash used in investing activities for the
fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, was $93,401. This was comprised of $65,315 for the purchase of mining claims and $28,086 for the
purchase of equipment. Net cash used in investing activities for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, was $46,610 for the purchase
of additional mining claims.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash provided by investing activities for
the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $0. Net cash used in investing activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2025,
of $116,011 this was a result of the purchase of mining claims and the purchase of equipment. The difference in investing activities between
September 30, 2025, and December 31, 2025, was attributed to the write of mining claims in the amount of $28,664 and shipping costs associated
with the purchase of equipment in the amount of $6,054.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Financing Activities</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash provided by financing activities was
$1,050,419 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, which consisted of $47,419 of proceeds from notes payable, $1,003,000 of net proceeds
from the sale of preferred stock. Net cash provided by financing activities was $204,581 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024,
which consisted of $204,581 of proceeds from notes payable from a related party.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Net cash provided by financing activities was
$66,863 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which consisted of $66,863 of net proceeds, comprised of Company expenses paid by
the Company&rsquo;s CEO. Net cash provided by financing activities was $1,030,383 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, which
consisted of $1,003,000 proceeds from the sale of Series A Super Voting Preferred Stock, and $27,383 net proceeds from expenses paid by
our CEO on behalf of the Company.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>
