<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The notes issued in 2017, 2021 and 2022 each matured
on December 31, 2023, and remain outstanding. The 2017 and 2021 notes are convertible at $0.005 per share, while the 2022 note is convertible
at $0.08 per share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On December 31, 2023, the Company issued a new
convertible promissory note to Shayla Investments LLC in the principal amount of $46,867. The note bears interest at 8%, is convertible
into common stock at $0.08 per share, and matures on December 31, 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On December 31, 2024, the Company issued a new
convertible promissory note to Shayla Investments LLC in the principal amount of $205,113. The note bears interest at 8%, is convertible
into common stock at $0.08 per share, and matures on December 31, 2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On December 31, 2025, the Company issued a new
convertible promissory note to Shayla Investments LLC in the principal amount of $47,020. The note bears interest at 8%, is convertible
into common stock at $0.08 per share, and matures on December 31, 2026.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The notes provide that, upon an event of default,
the lender may declare the outstanding principal, accrued interest and other amounts immediately due and payable. The notes are unsecured
and do not bear a separate default interest rate.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Shayla Investments LLC is considered a related
party because Mac Shahsavar is the Managing Member of Shayla Investments LLC and is also the Company&rsquo;s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company
had related-party notes payable of $452,668 and $405,249, respectively, and accrued interest of $93,756 and $61,344, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 5 &mdash; Related Party Transactions</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s Chairman and Chief Executive
Officer has provided funding to support the Company&rsquo;s ongoing operations through Shayla Investments LLC, a limited liability company
owned by the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. Amounts advanced are related-party transactions and may be settled in cash or, where
permitted by the applicable agreement and U.S. GAAP, through the issuance of the Company&rsquo;s capital stock. Expenses incurred on behalf
of the Company in the ordinary course of Company business are eligible for reimbursement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2025, the Company had no compensation
agreements or arrangements with its directors or officers other than transactions otherwise disclosed in these financial statements. For
additional information regarding the Company&rsquo;s related-party notes payable and accrued interest, see Note 4 &mdash; Notes Payable
and Accrued Interest &mdash; Related Party.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 6 &mdash; Mineral Properties and Exploration
Activities</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is an exploration-stage mining company
focused on the exploration and development of mineral properties, including properties projective for antimony. The Company has not commenced
commercial production and, accordingly, has not generated revenue from the sale of minerals.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Mineral Properties</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Mineral property costs consist primarily of costs
incurred to acquire and maintain mineral claims and other mineral property interests. The Company capitalizes acquisition costs of mineral
properties when the applicable criteria for capitalization under U.S. GAAP are met. Exploration and evaluation expenditures incurred prior
to establishing the technical feasibility and commercial viability of mineral properties are expensed as incurred unless such costs qualify
for capitalization under applicable U.S. GAAP.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s mineral properties primarily relate
to the American Antimony Project, Stibium Creek Property and Crystalite Project. Mineral property costs consist primarily of costs incurred
to acquire and maintain mineral claims and other mineral property interests.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 54; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->12<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">During 2024, the
Company had 79 American Antimony Project claims at the beginning of the year, acquired 124 additional claims, and wrote off or disposed
of two claims, resulting in 201 claims</FONT> at December 31, 2024. <FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">Additions to mineral properties during
2024 were $52,702, primarily related to the acquisition and maintenance of additional American Antimony Project claims. The Company recognized
a $1,092 write-off related to two mining claims that were no longer active.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-size: 10pt"></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company did not hold any Stibium Creek Property
or Crystalite Project claims during 2024. Accordingly, the carrying amount of mineral properties was $137,302 at December 31, 2024, compared
with $85,692 at December 31, 2023.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During 2025, the Company had 201 American Antimony
Project claims at the beginning of the year and ended the year with 201 claims. The Company acquired 60 Stibium Creek Property claims
and 97 Crystalite Project claims during 2025 and subsequently wrote off 57 Crystalite Project claims, resulting in 60 Stibium Creek Property
claims and 40 Crystalite Project claims at December 31, 2025. The Company incurred $93,979 of additions to mineral properties during 2025,
consisting of $11,223 related to the American Antimony Project, $33,977 related to the Stibium Creek Property and $48,779 related to the
Crystalite Project. The Company recognized an impairment/write-off of $28,664 related to the 57 Crystalite Project claims during 2025.
Accordingly, the carrying amount of mineral properties was $202,617 at December 31, 2025, compared with $137,302 at December 31, 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Exploration Activities</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is currently in the exploration stage
and has not established the commercial viability of its mineral properties. Exploration and evaluation activities are undertaken to assess
the mineral potential and economic viability of the Company&rsquo;s properties. Costs associated with exploration activities that do not meet
the criteria for capitalization are expensed as incurred.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company expects to incur additional exploration
and evaluation expenditures as it continues to assess its mineral properties. There can be no assurance that the Company&rsquo;s exploration
activities will result in the discovery of commercially viable mineral deposits or that the Company&rsquo;s mineral properties will ultimately
be developed into producing properties.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Impairment and Write-off of Mineral Properties</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company evaluates its mineral properties for
impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of a mineral property may not be recoverable. When
the carrying amount of a mineral property is determined to be impaired, the Company recognizes an impairment loss in accordance with applicable
U.S. GAAP.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During 2025, the Company recognized an impairment/write-off
of $28,664 related to 57 claims associated with the Crystalite Project. During 2024, the Company recognized a $1,092 write-off related
to two mining claims associated with the American Antimony Project that were no longer active.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result of these impairment and write-off
activities, the carrying amount of mineral properties was $202,617 and $137,302 as of December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 7 &mdash; Fair Value of Financial Instruments</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s financial instruments consist primarily
of cash, accounts payable, accrued liabilities, notes payable and accrued interest. The carrying amounts of cash, accounts payable and
accrued liabilities approximate their fair values due to the short-term nature of these instruments. The Company&rsquo;s related-party notes
payable are carried at their principal amounts, together with accrued interest, in accordance with the applicable U.S. GAAP guidance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has not elected to measure these instruments
at fair value. The Company evaluates the fair value of financial instruments in accordance with ASC 820, Fair Value Measurement, and ASC
825, Financial Instruments. There were no financial instruments measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of December 31, 2025 and
2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 8 &mdash; Earnings Per Share</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Basic earnings per share (&ldquo;EPS&rdquo;) is
calculated by dividing net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during
the period. Diluted EPS is calculated using the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding and, when applicable, the dilutive
effect of potentially issuable common shares. Because the Company reported net losses for the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024,
potentially dilutive securities were excluded from the calculation of diluted EPS because their inclusion would have been antidilutive.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The following table presents the calculation of
basic and diluted loss per share for the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 9 &mdash; Commitments and Contingencies</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Legal Proceeding</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is, from time to time, subject to
claims and legal proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business. The Company evaluates contingencies in accordance with ASC 450,
<I>Contingencies</I>, and recognizes a liability when a loss is probable and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On December 20, 2023, the Company filed a complaint
in the Eighth Circuit Court for Davidson County, Tennessee (Case No. 23C2957) against eight defendants relating to 15.24 million shares
of the Company&rsquo;s common stock issued in 2012 in connection with services to be provided by Anglo-African Mining. The arrangement
was terminated prior to the performance of the contemplated services. The Company alleged that, because the services were not rendered,
the shares were required to be returned to the Company and that the related share issuances should be canceled.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company sought a determination from the court
that the defendants had no right, title, or interest in the shares and that the Company was authorized to cancel the related share issuances.
The defendants were served with the complaint but did not respond.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On October 1, 2024, the Court entered an order
granting the Company&rsquo;s motion for default with respect to one of the defendants, resulting in the cancellation of 3.0 million shares
held by that defendant. As of the date of this report, no additional claim, order, judgment, or settlement has been entered by the Court
with respect to the remaining defendants.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On August 18, 2025, the Company&rsquo;s Board
of Directors determined that the proposed transaction pursuant to which the 15.24 million shares were issued should be canceled because
the contemplated services were not rendered by the defendants.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Based on the court-ordered cancellation of the
3.0 million shares, the failure of the remaining defendants to respond to the Company&rsquo;s complaint, and the Company&rsquo;s interpretation
of Wyoming Statute &sect; 17-16-621, relating to the issuance of shares for services not performed, hence, the Board of Directors authorized
the cancellation of all 15.24 million shares originally issued in connection with the arrangement. The canceled shares were returned to
the status of authorized and unissued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company intends to pursue any available legal
remedies in the event any of the remaining defendants assert a claim to or otherwise challenge the Company&rsquo;s cancellation of the
shares. The Company believes that it has a valid basis for the cancellation of the shares; however, there can be no assurance that the
Company will prevail in any future litigation or proceedings relating to the shares.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Settlement Agreement</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On June 1, 2025, the Company entered into a Settlement
and Release Agreement with certain parties involved in the proceeding. Under the agreement, the parties agreed to a full and final settlement
and mutual release of claims arising through the date of the agreement. As part of the settlement, the Company agreed to pay $8,290.56
and issue 4,816,545 restricted shares of Common Stock. The agreement also provides for the delivery of certain historical exploration
and property records.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2025, management believes the
matter has been resolved, subject to the Company&rsquo;s remaining obligations under the settlement agreement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Commitments and Contingencies</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company may enter into contractual arrangements
that require future payments, equity issuances or other performance obligations. The Company evaluates such arrangements to determine
whether they meet the recognition and disclosure requirements under U.S. GAAP.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2025, the Company&rsquo;s principal
commitments and contingencies consisted of the obligations arising under the Settlement and Release Agreement described above.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company had no other material commitments,
guarantees or loss contingencies requiring recognition or disclosure in the accompanying financial statements, other than those described
herein.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 10 &mdash; Income Taxes</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company did not recognize a provision for,
or benefit from, income taxes for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">At December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had
deferred tax assets principally arising from net operating loss carryforwards. The deferred tax amounts were measured using the enacted
U.S. federal corporate income tax rate of 21%. Based on the Company&rsquo;s tax calculation, the federal net operating loss carryforward was
$4,963,040 at December 31, 2025 and $1,796,446 at December 31, 2024, resulting in federal deferred tax assets of $1,042,238 and $377,254,
respectively. Because management has concluded that it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be realized, the
Company recorded a valuation allowance equal to 100% of its deferred tax assets at December 31, 2025 and 2024.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is domiciled in Wyoming and has mineral
properties in Nevada and Washington. Based on the jurisdictions identified in the financial statements, no state corporate income tax
has been included in the deferred tax calculation. Accordingly, the applicable tax rate used in measuring the deferred tax assets is 21%
for U.S. federal income tax.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 58; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->16<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Due to the changes in the Tax Reform Act of 1986
and the Tax Cut and Jobs Act of 2017, net operating loss carry forwards of Federal Income tax reporting purposes are subject to additional
limitations. Should certainly changes in ownership occur, our net operating loss carry forwards may be limited to use in future years.
In addition, tax rates on corporations were reduced and certain other deductions limited. These changes may affect the income tax benefit
calculation and related allowance during subsequent fiscal years.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The IRS requires domestic corporations to file
income tax returns for each tax year, regardless of taxable income. The Company has not filed income tax returns since inception, including
the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, during which it incurred losses. The Company has not received any notifications from
the IRS. Reported tax benefits and valuation allowances represent management&rsquo;s best estimate of its tax positions and have not been
reviewed by taxing authorities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 11 &mdash; Stockholders&rsquo; Equity</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s authorized capital consists
of unlimited shares of Common Stock and 500,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock of which the Series A Preferred Stock has designated share
capital of 5,000,000 shares, each with a par value of $0.0001 per share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Each share of Series A Preferred Stock carries
20,000 votes and is convertible into 2,000 shares of Common Stock. The Series A Preferred Stock is non-redeemable and non-callable. The
Company evaluated the terms and features of the Series A Preferred Stock under applicable U.S. GAAP and determined that separate derivative
accounting and mezzanine or temporary equity classification were not required. Accordingly, the Series A Preferred Stock is presented
within stockholders&rsquo; equity.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During 2025, the Company issued 7,466,545 shares
of Common Stock to five unrelated parties for services rendered. During 2024, the Company issued 1,000,000 shares of Common Stock to two
individuals for services rendered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On August 27, 2025, following receipt of a court
order in favour of the Company, the Company cancelled an aggregate of 15,240,000 shares of Common Stock. The shares had originally been
issued in 2011 as a finder&rsquo;s fee in connection with a transaction that was subsequently terminated. The consideration for the services
to be performed had a fair value of approximately $8,493. The cancellation was reflected in stockholders&rsquo; equity in accordance with
the Company&rsquo;s accounting records and the applicable court order.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On February 2, 2025, the Company issued 57,000
shares of Series A Preferred Stock for services rendered. Based on an independent valuation, the fair value of these shares was determined
to be $3.20 per share, resulting in aggregate compensation expense of $182,400. During March to July, the Company issued 6,269 shares
of Series A Preferred Stock to investors for cash consideration of $160 per share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During 2024, the Company issued 2,500 shares of
Series A Preferred Stock to five individuals in connection with the acquisition of four additional mining claims. Based on an independent
evaluation, the transaction was valued at $5,000.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2025, the Company had 217,778,045
shares of Common Stock and 1,266,769 shares of Series A Preferred Stock issued and outstanding. As of December 31, 2024, the Company had
225,551,500 shares of Common Stock and 1,203,500 shares of Series A Preferred Stock issued and outstanding.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The potential common shares issuable upon conversion
of the Series A Preferred Stock are considered in the Company&rsquo;s diluted earnings-per-share calculation. Because the Company reported
net losses for the periods presented, the potential common shares were excluded from diluted loss per share because their effect would
have been antidilutive.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 12 &mdash; Subsequent Events</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company evaluated events and transactions
occurring after December 31, 2025 through the date the financial statements were issued for potential recognition or disclosure in accordance
with ASC 855, Subsequent Events.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On January 9, 2026, the Company issued a total
of 100 shares of Series A Preferred Stock to two individuals for services rendered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On May 6, 2026, the Company issued a total of
25 shares of Series A Preferred Stock to one individual for services rendered.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">On August 18, 2026, the Company paid and filed
its annual maintenance fees with the Bureau of Land Management, maintaining the applicable claims in good standing. The next annual maintenance
payment is due on or before September 1, 2027.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><B>XTRA
ENERGY CORPORATION</B><BR>
<B><A NAME="a_011"></A>Notes to the Financial Statements<BR>
</B>For the Three and Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 and 2025</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Note 1 &mdash; Nature of Business and Operations</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Xtra Energy Corporation (the &ldquo;Company&rdquo;)
was originally incorporated in Nevada under the name Turner Group, Inc. In April 1999, the Company changed its name to AutoAuction.com,
Inc. In January 2005, the Company redomiciled its corporate jurisdiction from Nevada to Wyoming and subsequently changed its name to HLV
Trading Corp. in March 2005. In August 2006, the Company changed its name to X-Tra Petroleum, and in November 2010 changed its name to
Xtra Energy Corporation, which remains its current name.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company initially acquired 825 acres comprising
40 mineral claims. The Company subsequently acquired an additional 3,588 acres comprising 161 claims, bringing this claim group to 201
claims covering approximately 4,153 acres. In addition, the Company acquired 40 claims in Okanogan County, Washington and 60 claims in
Lander County, Nevada.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is an exploration stage company, engaged
in the exploration and development of mineral properties, principally targeting antimony. Antimony is an industrial semi-metal used in,
among other applications, batteries, semiconductors, flame-retardant materials, paints and enamels. More than five past-producing mines
are located on the Company&rsquo;s claims.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 2 &mdash; Significant Accounting Policies</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Basis of Presentation</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The accompanying financial statements have been
prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America of (&ldquo;US GAAP&rdquo;) as found
in the Accounting Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;), and the Accounting Standards Update (&ldquo;ASU&rdquo;) of the Financial
Accounting Standards Board (&ldquo;FASB&rdquo;) and are expressed in US Dollars. The financial statements should be read in conjunction
with the notes contained herein as part of the Company&rsquo;s Form 10 filing under the Securities Exchange Commission. The following
is a summary of significant accounting policies applicable to the Company. The Company&rsquo;s fiscal year ends on December 31.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Use of Estimates</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The preparation of financial statements in conformity
with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure
of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and reported amounts of expenses during the reporting period.
Significant estimates and judgments include, among other matters, stock-based compensation, valuation of financial instruments, recoverability
of mineral property interests, and valuation allowances for deferred tax assets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Management bases its estimates and assumptions
on current facts, historical experience and other factors believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ
materially from those estimates, and revisions to estimates are recognized prospectively in the period in which the estimates are revised.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Cash and cash equivalents include short-term,
highly liquid investments, such as cash on account with commercial banks, certificates of deposit or money market funds that are readily
convertible to known amounts of cash and have original maturities of 90 days or less. All cash balances are held by major banking institutions.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Mineral Properties</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company is an exploration-stage mining company
engaged in the exploration and evaluation of mineral properties and has not established any proven or probable mineral reserves or commenced
commercial production.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Costs incurred to acquire mineral property interests,
including mineral claims and other rights to explore for and develop mineral deposits, are capitalized when the Company obtains the applicable
legal rights and the costs meet the recognition criteria under U.S. GAAP. Such costs may include direct acquisition costs, staking and
filing fees, and other costs directly attributable to obtaining mineral property interests.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 65; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->23<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Exploration and evaluation expenditures incurred
during the exploration stage are expensed as incurred. Such expenditures include geological and geophysical studies, sampling, drilling,
assaying, exploration labour, and other costs incurred to evaluate the existence, location, quantity, grade, or economic potential of
mineral deposits. Costs incurred to maintain and retain mineral properties during the exploration stage are also expensed as incurred,
unless such costs qualify for capitalization under applicable U.S. GAAP.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Capitalized mineral property acquisition costs
are not amortized while the properties remain in the exploration stage. The Company evaluates its capitalized mineral property interests
for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable. Such events or circumstances
may include the abandonment, expiration, or relinquishment of mineral claims; unsuccessful exploration results; significant adverse changes
in the Company&rsquo;s plans or ability to develop the properties; or other factors indicating that the carrying amount may not be recoverable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">When the Company determines that a mineral property
has no future economic benefit, the related capitalized costs are written off in the period such determination is made. If a property
advances to the development or production stage, subsequent expenditures will be accounted for in accordance with the applicable U.S.
GAAP guidance for development and production-stage mining activities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Fixed assets</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Property and equipment are recorded at cost, net
of accumulated depreciation and amortization. Property and equipment generally include purchases of items with a per-unit value greater
than $1,000 and an estimated useful life greater than one year. Depreciation and amortization are computed on a straight-line basis over
the estimated useful lives of the assets. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the related lease terms or their estimated
useful lives.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Contingent Liabilities</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company accounts for its contingent liabilities
in accordance with ASC 450 &ldquo;Contingencies&rdquo;. A provision is recorded when it is both probable that a liability has been incurred
and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">With respect to legal matters, provisions are
reviewed, and financial information is adjusted to reflect the impact of negotiations, estimated settlements, legal rulings, advice of
legal counsel and other information and events pertaining to a particular matter.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Related party disclosures</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Under ASC 850 &ldquo;Related Party Transactions,&rdquo;
an entity or person is considered to be a &ldquo;related party&rdquo; if it has control, significant influence or is a key member of management
or personnel. A transaction is considered to be a related party transaction when there is a transfer of resources or obligations between
related parties. The Company in accordance with the standard ASC 850 presents disclosures about related party transactions and outstanding
balances with related parties. See Notes 4 and 5.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Basic and diluted earnings per share</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company computes earnings per share in accordance
with ASC 260, &ldquo;Earnings Per Share.&rdquo; Basic EPS is calculated by dividing the income available to common stockholders by the
weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted EPS reflects the potential dilution that could occur if
securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Instruments that could potentially dilute basic
EPS in the future, such as stock options, unvested restricted shares, and convertible debt, are included in the computation of diluted
EPS. However, these instruments are excluded from the calculation of diluted EPS if their effect is anti-dilutive. An instrument is considered
anti-dilutive when its inclusion increases EPS or decreases the loss per share from continuing operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>&nbsp;</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Foreign Currency</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s functional and reporting currency
is the U.S. dollar. Transactions denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar are remeasured into U.S. dollars in accordance with
ASC 830, Foreign Currency Matters. Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are remeasured using exchange rates
in effect at the balance sheet date and resulting transaction gains and losses are recognized in the statements of operations.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Revenue Recognition</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with
Accounting Standards Codification (&ldquo;ASC&rdquo;) 606, <I>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</I>. The core principle of ASC 606
is that revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration
to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company applies the following five-step model
in determining revenue recognition:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD STYLE="width: 3%">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 3%">1.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 94%">Identify the contract with a customer;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">2.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Identify the performance obligations in the contract;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">3.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Determine the transaction price;</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">4.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations; and</TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
    <TD>&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">5.</TD>
    <TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Recognize revenue when, or as, the Company satisfies a performance obligation.</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The transaction price represents the amount of
consideration to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring promised goods or services to a customer. The transaction
price may include fixed consideration, variable consideration, or both. When determining the transaction price, the Company considers,
as applicable, variable consideration, constraints on variable consideration, significant financing components, noncash consideration,
and consideration payable to a customer.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Mineral and Antimony Sales</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">When the Company commences commercial production
and enters into contracts with customers for the sale of antimony or other mineral products, revenue will be recognized when control of
the products transfers to the customer in accordance with the applicable contractual terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The transfer of control will generally occur upon
delivery of the mineral products to the customer or other point specified in the contract when the customer obtains the ability to direct
the use of and obtain substantially all of the remaining benefits from the products.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company will consider the specific terms of
each sales arrangement in determining the appropriate point of revenue recognition, including delivery terms, acceptance provisions, rights
of return, pricing provisions, and other contractual terms.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 67; Value: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->25<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Variable Consideration</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Where consideration is subject to variability,
including adjustments based on the quantity, quality, grade, assay results, or other characteristics of mineral products, the Company
will estimate variable consideration in accordance with ASC 606 and include amounts in the transaction price only to the extent that it
is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur when the uncertainty is subsequently resolved.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Royalties, Streaming and Other Mineral-Related
Arrangements</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">If the Company enters into royalty, streaming,
offtake, joint marketing, processing, or other arrangements involving mineral properties or mineral products, the Company will evaluate
each arrangement to determine whether it represents a contract with a customer within the scope of ASC 606 or is subject to other applicable
U.S. GAAP guidance. Revenue will be recognized based on the applicable accounting guidance and the specific contractual terms of the arrangement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><U>Contract Balances</U></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Amounts received from customers before the Company
satisfies the related performance obligations will be recorded as contract liabilities or deferred revenue, as applicable. Amounts for
which the Company has an unconditional right to consideration will be recorded as accounts receivable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company had no revenue from contracts with
customers during the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Income Taxes</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company accounts for income taxes using the
asset-and-liability method in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the estimated
future tax consequences of temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of assets and liabilities and their
respective tax bases, as well as for net operating loss and tax credit carry forwards.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation
allowance when, based on the weight of available evidence, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets
will not be realized. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in
the periods in which the temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effects of changes in tax rates are recognized
in income in the period in which the change in tax law is enacted.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recognizes the financial statement
benefit of an uncertain tax position only when it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, based
on the technical merits of the position. The amount of tax benefit recognized is measured as the largest amount of benefit that is greater
than 50% likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company recognizes interest and penalties
related to uncertain tax positions, if applicable, as a component of income tax expense.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Stock-Based Compensation</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company accounts for share-based payments
in accordance with ASC 718, Compensation&mdash;Stock Compensation. Equity-classified awards are measured at fair value on the grant date
and recognized as compensation cost over the requisite service period. The fair value of stock options, when applicable, is estimated
using an appropriate option-pricing model, such as the Black-Scholes model. Awards of common stock are measured using the fair value of
the Company&rsquo;s common stock on the applicable measurement date. Awards involving preferred stock are measured in accordance with
the applicable U.S. GAAP measurement guidance based on the facts and circumstances of the award. When observable market prices are not
available, the Company may use an independent valuation or other appropriate valuation technique to estimate fair value.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="width: 33%">&#160;</td><td style="width: 34%; text-align: center">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->26<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td><td style="width: 33%; text-align: right">&#160;</td></tr></table></DIV>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Fair value of financial instruments</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In accordance with ASC 820, Fair Value Measurement,
the Company categorizes financial instruments in a &lsquo;fair value hierarchy&rsquo;. The hierarchy categorizes the inputs used in valuation techniques
into three levels. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to (unadjusted) quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities
and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The following are the three categories related to the fair value measurement of such assets
or liabilities:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 1 inputs are quoted prices in active markets
for identical assets or liabilities that the Company can access at the measurement date, it holds a position in a single asset or liability
and the asset or liability is traded in an active market.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 2 inputs are inputs other than quoted market
prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Inputs are derived principally
from or corroborated by observable market data by correlation or other means (&lsquo;market-corroborated inputs&rsquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 3 inputs are unobservable for the asset
or liability. An entity develops unobservable inputs using the best information available in the circumstances, which might include the
entity&rsquo;s own data, taking into account all information about market participant assumptions that is reasonably available.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The classification of a fair value measurement
within the hierarchy is based on the lowest-level input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The carrying amounts of the Company&rsquo;s financial
instruments, including cash, accounts payable, accrued interest, and notes payable, approximate their fair values due primarily to the
short-term nature or other applicable terms of these instruments. As of September 30, 2026, and 2025, the Company had no assets or liabilities
that were required to be measured at fair value on a recurring basis. Accordingly, there were no assets or liabilities classified within
Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy as of September 30, 2026, or 2025.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Convertible Financial Instruments and Derivative
Features</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company evaluates the terms of its convertible
financial instruments to determine whether embedded features require separate accounting as derivative instruments under ASC 815, <I>Derivatives
and Hedging</I>. An embedded feature is bifurcated from its host contract when the applicable criteria for derivative accounting are met,
and the feature does not qualify for an available scope exception.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company evaluates conversion features to determine
whether they meet the definition of a derivative and whether they qualify for the applicable scope exception for contracts in the Company&rsquo;s
own equity under ASC 815-40.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Based on the Company&rsquo;s evaluation of its convertible
financial instruments, the embedded conversion features did not require separate accounting as derivative liabilities as of September
30, 2026, and 2025. Accordingly, no derivative liabilities were recognized in the accompanying financial statements.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">When an embedded feature is required to be accounted
for separately as a derivative, the derivative is initially measured at fair value and subsequently remeasured at fair value at each reporting
date, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings unless otherwise required by U.S. GAAP.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03,
Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40) - Companies must break out major expense categories (e.g., labour, depreciation)
in the notes to financial statements aimed at improving transparency. Effective for annual periods after Dec 15, 2026 (early adoption
allowed). This is applicable to the Company but it&rsquo;s not yet effective and the Company has not elected early adoption and currently
evaluating the impact.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Business segments</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company uses the &ldquo;management approach&rdquo;
to identify its reportable segments. The management approach designates the internal organization used by management for making operating
decisions and assessing performance as the basis for identifying the Company&rsquo;s reportable segments. Using the management approach, the
Company determined that it has one operating segment.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B><I>Subsequent Events</I></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company follows the guidance in ASC 855-10-50
of the FASB Accounting Standards Codification for the disclosure of subsequent events. The Company will evaluate subsequent events through
the date when the financial statements were issued. Pursuant to ASU 2010-09 of the FASB Accounting Standards Codification, the Company
as an SEC filer considers its financial statements issued when they are widely distributed to users, such as through filing them on EDGAR.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Note 3 &mdash; Going Concern</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The accompanying financial statements have been
prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern, which contemplates the continuity of operations, realization of assets
and settlement of liabilities in the normal course of business.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As reflected in the financial statements, the
Company had an accumulated deficit of $5,253,235 as of September 30, 2026 and $3,010,108 as of September 30, 2025. The Company incurred
net losses of $156,692 and $1,552,739 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Net cash used in operating
activities was $257,126 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and $655,395 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The Company
has not generated revenue. In addition, as of September 30, 2026, the Company had current liabilities of $656,865 compared with current
assets of $39,938 and a working capital deficit of $616,927. These conditions, along with the Company&rsquo;s recurring losses, accumulated
deficit, negative operating cash flows, and lack of revenue, raise substantial doubt about the Company&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going
concern.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Management intends to continue implementing the
Company&rsquo;s business plan and to seek additional capital through private or public equity offerings, debt financing, or a combination
thereof. The Company&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern is dependent on its ability to obtain adequate financing and, ultimately,
to generate sufficient cash flows from operations. Management&rsquo;s plans are intended to provide the Company with sufficient liquidity to
fund its operations and pursue its exploration activities; however, there can be no assurance that the Company will be successful in obtaining
additional financing or generating sufficient cash flows from operations. There can be no assurance that additional financing will be
available on acceptable terms, or at all.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As a result, management has concluded that its
plans do not alleviate substantial doubt about the Company&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern for a period of one year from the
date the financial statements are issued.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The financial statements do not include adjustments
to the recoverability or classification of recorded assets or to the amounts or classification of liabilities that might be necessary
if the Company is unable to continue as a going concern.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: left"><B>Note 4 &mdash; Notes Payable and Accrued Interest
&ndash; Related Party</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company has entered convertible promissory
notes with Shayla Investments LLC, a related party. The notes bear interest at 8% per annum, are unsecured, and provide the holder with
the option to convert outstanding principal and accrued interest into shares of the Company&rsquo;s common stock at the applicable conversion
price specified in each note.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The notes generally limit conversions to 4.99%
of the Company&rsquo;s issued and outstanding common stock per issuance. The notes also contain customary provisions relating to events of default,
acceleration, prepayment and anti-dilution.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"></P>
